content.title: Watch vs. Warning
content.text: It's not always easy to remember the difference between an event watch and a warning. We think there's no better way to demonstrate this concept than with the humble, yet delicious, taco! Watch: Hazardous conditions exist. Prepare for action. A watch is issued when conditions are likely to occur and create widespread impact on life and/or property. To revisit our taco analogy, we have the ingredients to make tacos. Prepare for the event by reviewing your safety plans, checking your emergency kits, and monitoring local alerts and warnings. Warning: Event is imminent. Take Action Now! A warning is issued when an event is occurring and poses an immediate threat to life and/or property. Take immediate action by initiating your safety plans and following the guidance of local officials. In other words, our tacos are ready! Advisory: Be aware. Exercise Caution For those of you looking for a bonus definition, an advisory is a less serious condition but one that requires you to exercise caution as it could cause serious inconvenience and may threaten life and/or property. Exercise caution and monitor local alerts and warnings. Maybe make sure those taco ingredients are on your shopping list! For more information, including fire weather, air quality, and more, visit the National Weather Service's Watch, Warning, and Advisory page.
